title: amosblomqvist/learnharness
body:
Agent harness for learning difficult things.

README 節錄： An agent harness for learning. Download · How it works · Documentation · Issues LearnHarness uses AI agents to plan and teach lessons from your current understanding to your goal. It builds a detailed picture of what you understand and how you reason. That picture is updated as you learn. Instead of just giving you an explanation, it uses your answers and thinking to decide what you need next. Teaching builds understanding one reasoning step at a time. Practice makes it usable. A persistent knowledge graph carries it across sessions. ## How it works 1. **Measure.** Before teaching, the agent finds where your understanding ends on each part the lesson depends on. Your answers, confidence, and thinking show it where to start. 2. **Plan.** It works out a dependency map from that starting point to your goal. You can see the plan, and the lesson adapts when your understanding turns out different. 3. **Teach.** Each step builds on something you already understand. You predict, get an explanation, and check your understanding. Confusions are repaired before anything is built on them. The aim is for the goal to feel obviously true, not merely familiar. 4. **Practice.** Separate sessions pose varied problems that require the right knowledge to come to mind without being named first. title: EthanArbuckle/fairplay-decrypt
body:
Offline FairPlay App Store IPA decryption with independent key derivation

README 節錄：# IPA decryptor Decrypt FairPlay-encrypted apps using a 16-byte credential for the account that owns each IPA. Credential retrieval gets it from a supported jailbroken device and writes `credential.bin` to the chosen output directory. Decryption runs on macOS and Linux. Supports version-3 and version-5 SUPF, 448-byte and 440-byte SINF `priv` records, and encrypted arm64 Mach-O slices. A 440-byte record must end in eight zero bytes. ## Set up From this directory, with Python 3.9+: ```sh python3 -m venv .venv . .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -r requirements.txt ``` The decryptor is pure Python. On macOS, `make` builds the credential-retrieval bundle and requires Xcode and `ldid`. ## Decrypt ```sh python decrypt.py /path/to/encrypted.ipa /path/to/decrypted.ipa \ --credential /path/to/credential.bin ``` If `--credential` is omitted, the tool reads `./credential.bin`. The output path must not exist. The decryptor uses each IPA's SINF and SUPF records to derive page keys, decrypt its encrypted arm64 pages, and clear `cryptid`.

title: xevrion/hatchzip
body:
Extract huge archives in place: the archive shrinks as your files hatch, so you only need room for the output. ZIP, 7z, tar, split archives.

README 節錄： HatchZip Extract huge archives in place. The archive shrinks as your files hatch, so you only need free space for the output, not for the output and the archive. Installation | Usage | Safety | How it works | Contributing A 180 GB game download that unpacks to 200 GB needs 380 GB of disk with WinRAR, 7-Zip or `unzip`, because the archive and everything extracted from it have to exist at the same time. HatchZip needs a little over 200 GB. It extracts the archive from the end and cuts each finished part off the archive file as it goes, so the space the archive gives back is reused for the next files. It checks that the extraction will fit before it changes anything, keeps a safety margin of free space the whole way through, and can be stopped or crash at any moment and pick up where it left off. It reads ZIP, 7z, tar, `.tar.gz`, RAR volume sets and split archives. ### Get it > [!IMPORTANT] > HatchZip is only distributed from this repository's releases and its site, hatchzip.dev. Other sites using the name, such as hatchzip.com, are not affiliated with this project. No coding needed. **Download for Windows** (Windows 10 and 11), or for macOS (Apple Silicon), macOS (Intel) and Linux. 1. Run the installer. Windows may show "Windows protected your PC" because HatchZip is not code-signed yet: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway*

README 節錄： ### GPT-6 made computer use the frontier. We make it open. News · Results · Demos · **Quick start** · SDK · Open stack · How it works · Contributing · Contact **Computer use has reached a turning point.** GPT-6 Astra's demos offered an exciting vision of what computer-use agents could make possible, and the focus is expanding from GUI-only interaction to both visual and programmatic interfaces. The question has changed, from how well a model operates a GUI to how well a system completes work on a real computer by whatever means works. **We call such a system a generalist computer-use agent (GCUA).** It uses a computer in more ways than you do. It reads the accessibility tree and calls app APIs, runs shell commands, and operates the GUI when it needs to. With **code execution**, it writes GUI operations as code and combines them with all of these in one program, with loops and conditions. body: README 節錄：# HackiOS — XNU kernel **HackiOS** boots Apple's open-source **XNU kernel** (`xnu-8796.121.2`, the kernel of iOS 16.5) on Android phone hardware and runs the **unmodified iOS 16.5 user space** on top of it: launchd → backboardd → SpringBoard → apps. Our own EFI loader, our own replacements for Apple's closed drivers, a UEFI port, and a Linux Wi-Fi driver on a compatibility layer make that possible. It runs in two places: - **POCO X5 Pro 5G (redwood, Snapdragon 778G)** — nothing is flashed: the UEFI is started with `fastboot boot`, the whole system lives in RAM, and after a reboot the phone is back in Android; - **QEMU** (`virt`, aarch64) — the same thing on any Linux computer, no phone needed. This repository is half of the project: | Repository | What | |---|---| | **hackios-xnu-kernel** (this one) | XNU patches, the EFI loader, the UEFI port, Wi-Fi, QEMU scripts, `xl`, prebuilt kernel/loader/UEFI, `common/` scripts | | hackios-xnu-userland | our init, injected libraries, launchd jobs, the APFS image builder, the scripts that take iOS out of Apple's IPSW, Metal/Mesa work | > **No Apple files are in either repository.** `ios165/fetch.sh` downloads the iOS 16.5 IPSW from Apple's own CDN > to *your* machine and extracts what is needed there. Import .sql files into TypeScript with full type inference and zero codegen.

README 節錄： Import .sql files into your TypeScript code with full type inference Read the docs → If you have a file like this: ```sql -- get_author.sql select u.id, u.name, count(p.id)::int as post_count from users u left join posts p on p.user_id = u.id where u.id = :id::int group by u.id ``` You can import it directly from a TypeScript file like this: ```ts // main.ts import postgres from "postgres"; import getAuthor from "./get_author.sql"; const db = postgres(process.env.DATABASE_URL); const author = await getAuthor.run(db, { id: 1 }); // { id: number; name: string; post_count: number } | null ``` Reylo is powered by TypeScript content mappers, introduced in TypeScript 7.1 (currently in beta), which let you dynamically define static types for external file types and integrate them directly into TypeScript compilation. title: eagle-hq/EAGLE-4
body:
Official Inference Code of EAGLE-4

README 節錄： EAGLE-4 One Flexible Drafter for All Batch Sizes and Hardware Paper (EAGLE-4) · EAGLE-4 draft for Qwen3.8-27B · Documentation Figure 1(a) of the EAGLE-4 paper: Qwen3.8-27B on the SPEED-Bench qualitative split, 4× NVIDIA B300, one request, temperature 0. The numbers this release measured with EAGLE-4 are in the support matrix . ## EAGLE-4 **Leave speculation on. EAGLE-4 adapts to your hardware, batch and workload.** For high load, serve SGLang on four B300 GPUs with the high-load recipe, which keeps pace with plain decoding up to 512 concurrent requests. EAGLE-4 (Extrapolation Algorithm for Greater Language-model Efficiency) speeds up LLM inference with speculative decoding. EAGLE-4 draft models are built to run with `eagle-harness`, which decides how far to speculate from measured costs on your setup, so every draft tree fits the batch size, the hardware and the workload. The output stays exactly what the target model would generate on its own: up to 3.4× faster generation on Qwen3.8-27B, with the same answers. title: Snapintosh/Snapintosh
body:
EL2 hypervisor and toolchain that boots macOS on the ASUS A16 (Snapdragon X2 Elite), with an Adreno Metal/IOGPU stack

README 節錄：# Snapintosh Snapintosh boots Apple's macOS 27 (build 26A428) on an ASUS Zenbook A16 laptop with a Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite (X2E-96-100). It is an EL2 monitor (hypervisor) and the toolchain around it. The monitor runs Apple's stock kernelcache (the J700/T8140 kernel) unmodified by default. It supplies the platform contracts that the kernel expects from Apple silicon: the SPTM and TXM monitor calls, translation of the kernel's 16 KiB page tables, and the Apple devices the kernel looks for. Graphics run on the laptop's own Adreno X2-90 GPU through a driver stack written for this project: - **AdrenoMetal.bundle**: a Metal driver plug-in. - **AdrenoX2**: an IOGPU kernel extension, with **AdrenoDisplay** driving the internal panel. - **air2ir3**: a shader compiler that translates Apple's AIR (Metal's IR) into Mesa's ir3 for the Adreno. There is no software, CPU or paravirtual rendering path. The project also includes an I2C-HID keyboard and touchpad driver (SnapI2CHID), native QCC2072 Wi-Fi work, and NVMe storage through an emulated Apple storage controller. Snapintosh is used together with q1n1, a UEFI EL2 proxy forked from Asahi Linux's m1n1. q1n1 takes the machine at EL2 after UEFI and serves m1n1's proxy protocol over USB-C to a Mac host, which drives Snapintosh from there. ## Status This is experimental software, written for one laptop model. |

title: assetnote/php2shell-scanner
body:
High fidelity scanner for php2shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)

README 節錄：# php2shell-scanner A command-line tool for detecting CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 in PHP applications. ## How It Works The scanner sends a minimal multipart control request followed by up to three crafted multipart probes. The probes use PHP array keys nested 62 levels deep and increase from 1 MiB to 20 MiB, matching the detection logic used by Assetnote's internal scanner. A target is reported vulnerable when the probe produces a PHP memory-exhaustion error, a differential empty HTTP 500, a PHP-FPM worker failure, or an advertised PHP version known to be unpatched. Initial 5xx responses, common request-rejection statuses, and nonempty HTTP 500 responses without the PHP fatal-error signature are not treated as crash signals. The scanner tests `/index.php` by default. A path supplied in the URL is preserved, and `--path` or `--path-file` can test custom paths. phpMyAdmin targets are automatically retested at `/show_config_errors.php`. Redirects are not followed unless `--follow-redirects` is set. ### SAPI Modes The default `--sapi auto` mode applies both mod_php and PHP-FPM verdict rules, matching the combined behavior of Assetnote's postmodules. Use `--sapi mod_php` or `--sapi fpm` to restrict detection to a known SAPI. ### Network Impact Each tested path may receive a 42-byte control request and three probes totalling about 29 MiB. body: README 節錄： > **Coding agents:** skip this README and read AGENTS.md directly. Flare is a local inference server for NVIDIA SM120/SM121 GPUs, built for long conversations, coding agents, and repeated tool use. Its goal is to make the memory, bandwidth, and compute in workstations and compact systems such as DGX Spark go further, while keeping generation responsive. This is a research prototype, and is made available via open-source to enable technical collaboration and collect early feedback. The design rests on a few principles: - **Embrace the standard PyTorch ecosystem at build time; serve from Rust.** Ignition uses PyTorch, Transformers, and FlashInfer/b12x to load models, tune kernels, compile forwards, and capture CUDA graphs into a runtime package. Helios, the Rust runtime, serves that package without Python. Compilation and graph capture finish before serving. - **Build on the model ecosystem.** Reuse canonical model implementations wherever their dataflow fits, and specialize the parts that need different layouts or execution. Model development keeps the tools and libraries that make the Python ecosystem productive. - **Make memory and state explicit.** Plan buffers and execution capacities ahead of time. title: VictorTaelin/uniichat
body: README 節錄：UniiChat ======== ▶ Watch the announcement video **This repo is vibe-coded.** AI agents wrote nearly all of it, and AI agents reviewed it. Read it, run it and fork it as such: expect bugs. UniiChat is an AI agent with one chat that never ends. There is no "new chat" button: you talk to the same agent for days, weeks, years, and it remembers. The hosted version is at https://uniichat.com. This is its source, to run your own server on your own API keys. How it works ------------ - **One chat, a memory tree.** Every message is summarized into one line, and neighboring lines are merged in pairs, again and again, into a binary tree. Each call sees a view of the whole chat, up to 128 KB: recent messages one line each, older ones covered by fewer, broader lines. Detail fades with age, but nothing is lost. - **Zoom.** The agent can open any line into the two it was made from, down to the original message. So its context never rots, and it never needs a "compaction" that throws the past away. - **Built in the background.** Summaries are written by a cheaper model (the compactor) as messages arrive. The view changes only at its end, so each call reads most of its input from the vendor's prompt cache. - **Every window is a view.** The server owns the chat. A browser tab, or `unii` in a terminal, shows it live; any of them can send a message, stop the work, or change the model. - **Agents and tools.** The agent runs a shell, reads and edits files, and can drive a Mac's screen
